facts.statement: The holotype fossil, a partial left upper arm bone, was discovered by R.I. Smith near Sandsfoot in Dorset, England.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Duriatitan, BMNH 44635, is a partial left upper arm bone which was found by R.I. Smith near Sandsfoot, Weymouth in the lower Kimmeridge Clay from Dorset.

facts.statement: The species was originally described in 1874 by John Hulke as a species of Cetiosaurus.
facts.quote: The type species, D. humerocristatus, was described in 1874 by John Hulke as a species of Cetiosaurus

facts.statement: The specific name refers to the prominent deltopectoral crest on the humerus bone.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the deltopectoral crest, crista, on the upper arm bone, humerus.

facts.statement: The generic name is derived from the Latin name for Dorset and the Greek word for Titan.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del nombre en latín para Dorset, Duria y del griego Titan.

facts.statement: A distinctive feature is the long, sharply projecting deltopectoral crest.
facts.quote: Una característica distintiva es el peine deltopectoral largo y que sobresale agudamente.

facts.statement: The entire humerus is very strong, indicating that the front legs were longer than the hind legs.
facts.quote: Todo el húmero es muy fuerte, lo que indica que las patas delanteras eran más largas que las traseras.

facts.statement: The bone's construction led Hulke to defend the hypothesis that sauropods lived on land rather than in the sea, as was commonly believed at the time.
facts.quote: La construcción del hueso llevó a Hulke a defender la hipótesis existente de que los saurópodos vivían en tierra en lugar de en el mar, como se solía suponer en ese momento.

facts.statement: The humerus measures 137 cm without the missing central piece, with an estimated total length of 160 cm, indicating a body length of about 18 meters and a weight of 12 tons.
facts.quote: El húmero, que mide 137 centímetros de largo sin la pieza central que falta, tiene una longitud total estimada de alrededor de 160 centímetros, lo que indica una longitud corporal de unos 18 metros y un peso de 12 toneladas.

facts.statement: It lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 150 million years ago in the Kimmeridgian stage, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 150 millones de años durante el Kimmeridgiense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: The time range spans from the Kimmeridgian to the Berriasian, between 154.8 and 137.05 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Berriasian (154.8 to 137.05 million years ago)

facts.statement: According to the describers, it is a member of the Titanosauriformes, a group that includes both Brachiosauridae and Titanosauria.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con los descriptores, es un miembro de los Titanosauriformes , una amplia variedad que incluye tanto a Brachiosauridae como a Titanosauria

facts.statement: It is debated whether the animal belongs to the Brachiosauridae, as a 2007 hypothesis by Darren Naish and David Martill could not be supported by the describers with new features.
facts.quote: La hipótesis de Darren Naish y David Martill de 2007 de que el animal debería pertenecer a los Brachiosauridae no podría ser respaldada por los descriptores con nuevas características.

rejected.statement: The specimen was assigned to its own genus in 2010 by Paul M. Barrett, Roger B.J. Benson, and Paul Upchurch.
rejected.quote: The specimen was assigned to its own genus by Paul M. Barrett, Roger B.J. Benson and Paul Upchurch in 2010.
